parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime places every trans visitor inside a universal-exposure net with no fully working remedy: entry screening that treats document/appearance divergence as grounds to refuse a visa or pursue a lifetime fraud bar, a national facilities exclusion, and documented abusive national/immigration custody if detention occurs. The Division adds a minors' care ban with provider liability and a tipline, a custody care cutoff with no taper, and no gender-identity non-discrimination law; its courts upheld the care ban, so 'functioning courts' mitigate nothing here. Partial protections are documented (gender-identity hate-crime statute, sanctuary cities, enjoined orders, ongoing litigation) but do not neutralise the exposures. No criminal statute targeting trans people, no documented arrests or violence in this Division, and no execution pathway keep this out of the High band, but the entry/custody/facility exposures put it firmly in Elevated Risk. Adult alone: entry and custody exposure. Adult with minor: adds care interruption and tipline exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented national cable directs refusal where documents cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility; trans travellers report confiscated passports and stranding; allied governments issued advisories after detentions of neighbouring citizens over visa issues; trans athletes barred entry.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements and is never automatic; litigation against passport policy ongoing.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate to refusal, lifetime bar, or detention and thence into the hostile custody regime.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau mandates haircutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution for trans inmates; immigration custody documented with forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men; Division denies hormones to inmates with no taper plan.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor refused at entry or investigated for misrepresentation can enter national or Division custody where these practices operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity, reaching every visitor at federal buildings and airports; Division documents no bathroom ban of its own.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility exclusion is universal exposure for outed or outable visitors regardless of state-level law.

care_services.exposure: SAFE Act bans initiating hormones/blockers under 18, with provider licence loss and 15-year patient suits chilling provision; Medicaid bar for all ages; custody care cutoff with no taper; tipline invites reports of 'gender transition interventions'.
care_services.protection: Minors already in treatment may continue; two cities declared trans sanctuaries; adult care ban withdrawn nationally.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor needing refills faces provider refusal risk; guardians risk scrutiny via the tipline.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice-department reward memo references 'radical gender ideology'; enforcement directed at schools facilitating minor transitions; state tipline.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Documents state counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; some orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing raises discovery stakes and licenses discrimination without state recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban in force (upheld unanimously January 2026); permanence pursued via legislature and ballot initiative; sports ban excludes trans minors from school athletics; school-transition facilitation criminally prosecutable nationally; hospital-record subpoenas.
minors_guardians.protection: Continuation of existing treatment allowed; sanctuary cities; litigation ongoing.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces care denial, school exclusion, and potential inquiry; provider liability reaches the provider, forcing care interruption for the family.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No gender-identity non-discrimination law; no dated trans-violence incident with outcome documented in the Division — an open question, not evidence of safety; first known bathroom-law arrest occurred in a different state/province.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime statute explicitly covers gender identity; national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims have theoretical bias-crime recourse, but no documented enforcement record is provided either way.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Courts upheld the care ban, so judicial recourse validated the exposure rather than relieving it; oversight did not prevent custody care cutoff; passport suit unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Several national orders blocked or enjoined; legal-aid FAQ exists; sanctuary ordinances operate locally.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Practical exposure depends on which measures are operative at travel time; unknowns include Division screening practice and custody placement for short detentions.

anchor_checks.comparison: Worse on paper for custody (national/immigration custody abuse documented, care cutoff) but better overall: no cross-dressing statute, no documented raids or arrests in this Division, a gender-identity hate-crime statute, sanctuary cities, and no pattern of detention of visitors inside the Division. Sits above 0.25-C.

Comparable tier: universal-exposure document checks, possible detention, no execution pathway, inconsistent enforcement. This dossier is slightly worse at entry (documented detentions of foreign trans citizens, lifetime fraud bar) and on custody abuse, but offset by hate-crime law and sanctuary cities. Roughly level, marginally below.

Below 0.55-B: that anchor's worst outcome is administrative refusal and delay with functioning appeal desks; here a fraud finding can be a permanent ineligibility, and detention leads to documented beatings and sexual abuse rather than routine holding.

Materially below 0.75-C: that anchor has trained border officers, compensation for unlawful detention, and tribunals ordering release; here courts affirm hostile statutes, custody practices are abusive, and no working remedy is documented for facility exclusion or care denial.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime the traveller encounters is national-first: entry screening that can refuse, strand, or lifetime-bar a trans applicant on document grounds, a national facility exclusion, and a custody system with documented abuse — the tier-1 exposures of the precedence ladder. The Division adds no criminal statute and no documented arrests or violence of its own, which keeps street-level severity moderate, but it deepens exposure for travelling families (minors' care ban upheld through the highest court, provider liability, sports exclusion, tipline) and for anyone detained (care cutoff, no taper). Courts here enforced the hostile rules, so rule-of-law strength is liability, not recourse. Documented protections — hate-crime coverage, sanctuary cities, enjoined orders — reduce but do not offset the exposures. Net: Elevated Risk, upper-middle of the band; adult alone somewhat safer than a family with a trans minor.
